q: What is the main purpose of the Scope performance domain?
options: To deliver as many features as possible
To ensure the project includes all the work required, and only the work required
To finish the project as early as possible
To assign team members to activities
explanation: The Scope domain ensures that all required work is included and that no unnecessary work is performed, which protects cost, schedule and value.

q: Which statement describes product scope?
options: The work performed to deliver the result
The approved budget for the product
The features, functions and characteristics of the product, service or result
The list of project team members
explanation: Product scope describes the result itself: its features, functions and characteristics. Project scope is the work performed to deliver it.

q: Which three items make up the scope baseline?
options: Project scope statement, WBS and WBS dictionary
Project charter, scope statement and WBS
Requirements documentation, WBS and activity list
Scope management plan, scope statement and WBS
explanation: The scope baseline is the approved scope statement, the WBS and its WBS dictionary. The charter, requirements documentation and scope management plan are not part of it.

q: What is the lowest level of the work breakdown structure?
explanation: The work package is the lowest level of the WBS. Activities are created later, when work packages are decomposed for the schedule, and are not part of the WBS.

q: A project manager needs the detailed description, responsible organization and acceptance criteria of one WBS component. Where is this found?
explanation: The WBS dictionary supports the WBS with detailed information about each component, such as description of work, responsible organization, milestones and acceptance criteria.

q: A team starts with the project's major deliverables and keeps dividing them into smaller, more manageable parts. Which technique is used to create the WBS?
explanation: Decomposition divides and subdivides the project scope and deliverables into smaller, more manageable parts.

q: A reviewer finds that a WBS leaves out the project management work and includes a deliverable nobody asked for. What does the 100 percent rule say about the WBS?
options: The WBS includes all product and project work, with nothing left out and nothing extra
Every work package must be 100% complete and accepted before the next one is allowed to start
All team members must approve the WBS
The WBS must be finished before the charter is signed
explanation: The WBS represents all product and project work, including project management work. Lower levels roll up to higher levels, so nothing is left out and no extra work is performed.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 5, Decomposition; Practice Standard for Work Breakdown Structures, 2.3.1

links.label: Practice Standard for Work Breakdown Structures, 2.3.1

q: Which process produces the requirements documentation?
explanation: Elicit and Analyze Requirements (older name: Collect Requirements) determines, documents and manages stakeholder needs and requirements.

q: "The system must respond to a search within two seconds." What type of requirement is this?
explanation: Nonfunctional requirements specify how well the product must perform: performance, reliability, security and similar. Functional requirements describe what the product does.

q: Data conversion and user training needed to move from the old system to the new one are examples of:
explanation: Transition and readiness requirements describe temporary capabilities needed to move from the current state to the desired future state.

q: Late in a project a tester asks which business need a requirement came from and which deliverable satisfies it. Which document links each requirement from its origin to the deliverable that satisfies it?
explanation: The requirements traceability matrix is a grid that links requirements from their origin to the deliverables that satisfy them, and helps manage changes to product scope.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Requirements traceability matrix

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Requirements traceability matrix

q: A customer assumes that staff training is included in the project. The team replies that it was explicitly left out. Where are project exclusions documented?
explanation: The project scope statement includes the scope description, deliverables, acceptance criteria and project exclusions. Stating what is out of scope helps manage expectations.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Project scope statement

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Project scope statement

q: What does the scope management plan describe?
options: How the scope will be defined, developed, monitored, controlled and validated
The cost of each work package
explanation: The scope management plan describes how scope will be managed. It does not contain the scope itself, and it is not part of the scope baseline.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Scope management plan

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Scope management plan

q: The team has checked a deliverable and found it correct. The customer now inspects it and signs to accept it. Which process formalizes acceptance of the completed project deliverables?
explanation: Validate Scope formalizes acceptance of completed deliverables by the customer or sponsor. Its main output is accepted deliverables.

q: Which of the following is an output of Monitor and Control Scope and an input to Validate Scope?
explanation: Monitor and Control Scope checks deliverables for correctness and produces verified deliverables. These are the input to Validate Scope, which produces accepted deliverables.

q: During Validate Scope the customer refuses to accept a deliverable. What should the project manager do?
options: Close the phase and move on
Ask the sponsor to accept it instead
Remove the rejected deliverable from the approved scope baseline entirely
Document the reasons and raise a change request for defect repair
explanation: Deliverables that are not accepted are documented with the reasons, and a change request is raised to repair the defect. Change requests are an output of Validate Scope.

q: A developer adds an extra report that the customer never asked for, hoping to please them. This is an example of:
explanation: Gold plating is the team adding extras that were not requested. It is not acceptable: it uses time and money for work outside the approved scope.
ref: The Project Management Answer Book, Chapter 4, Q16

links.label: The Project Management Answer Book, Chapter 4, Q16

q: A stakeholder keeps asking team members for small additions. They are added without any review, and the project falls behind. What is this called?
explanation: Scope creep is the uncontrolled expansion of scope without adjusting time, cost and resources. It is prevented by sending every change through change control.

q: Which statement about a control account is correct?
options: It is a management control point where scope, budget and schedule are integrated and compared with earned value
It is the lowest level of the WBS
It is a bank account for project funds
It can belong to several work packages
explanation: A control account integrates scope, budget and schedule for performance measurement. It has two or more work packages, and each work package belongs to only one control account.

q: A team moving from a predictive to an adaptive approach asks where its scope will now be listed and ordered. In a project using an adaptive approach, what corresponds to the WBS?
explanation: In agile projects the WBS corresponds to the product backlog, where work items are broken down into epics, features and user stories.

q: What is the definition of done?
options: The date on which the project ends
A checklist of all the criteria a deliverable must meet to be considered ready for customer use
The sponsor's signature on the final report
The list of completed work packages
explanation: The definition of done is a checklist of all criteria that must be met so that a deliverable can be considered ready for customer use.

q: The team brainstorms ideas for requirements and then votes to rank them. Which technique is this?
explanation: The nominal group technique adds a voting step to brainstorming so that the ideas can be ranked and prioritized.

q: Which of the following does a work breakdown structure show?
options: The order in which the work packages will be carried out
The hierarchical breakdown of the total scope of work
The people assigned to each element
explanation: A WBS describes scope only. Its elements do not account for time or sequence, do not contain costs, do not assign resources and do not imply relationships or importance.
ref: Practice Standard for Work Breakdown Structures, 2.3.1

links.label: Practice Standard for Work Breakdown Structures, 2.3.1

q: While building a WBS, a team member suggests adding the element "Install the windows". How should this be handled?
options: Record the deliverable ("Windows") in the WBS; the activity belongs in the schedule
Reject it, because windows are not in scope
Add it twice, under two parents, to be safe
explanation: Activities are not part of the WBS: the WBS represents the what and activities represent the how. Suggested activities are translated into their deliverables.
ref: Practice Standard for Work Breakdown Structures, 2.3.1; Practice Standard for Work Breakdown Structures, 2.4.3

links.label: Practice Standard for Work Breakdown Structures, 2.3.1
